candidate.answerReason: The distinct Wednesday balances are 7, 8, and 10 dollars. Applying both allowed operations to each gives the six distinct Thursday balances 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, and 20 dollars.

methods.label: List the different balances day by day
methods.explanation:
Track the different balances each day, applying both allowed choices to every balance. If two paths reach the same balance, keep that balance only once: the next day's choices depend only on the money Taye currently has.

Starting with \(2\) dollars on Monday, Tuesday's possibilities are \(2+3=5\) and \(2\times2=4\) dollars.

On Wednesday, \(4\) dollars can become \(7\) or \(8\), while \(5\) dollars can become \(8\) or \(10\). Thus the distinct Wednesday balances are \(7\), \(8\), and \(10\) dollars.

Apply both choices once more for Thursday:
\[
\begin{aligned}
7&\longrightarrow 10\text{ or }14,\\
8&\longrightarrow 11\text{ or }16,\\
10&\longrightarrow 13\text{ or }20.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every possible balance is included because we applied both choices to every balance from the previous day. The resulting amounts are
\[
10,\ 11,\ 13,\ 14,\ 16,\ 20,
\]
with no repeats. There are \(6\) different amounts, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: This is elementary day-by-day enumeration using addition and doubling. The roster node describes listing distinct outcomes; formal set theory or recurrence formulas are unnecessary.
